claim: M1 macrophage activation is important for eradicating bacteria such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

claim: M1 macrophages favor near exclusive use of glycolysis.

claim: M. tuberculosis has arguably caused the most deaths of any pathogen in human history.

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to World Health Organization team, 2021.

claim: β-glucan training enhances mouse survival following in vivo M. tuberculosis infection.
source: Apart from the BCG vaccine, it has been demonstrated that other organisms and compounds can induce innate training, such as β-glucan (van der Meer et al., 2015) which induced protective innate training against virulent M. tuberculosis, as shown by enhanced mouse survival following in vivo infection, and enhanced human monocyte pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion following ex vivo infection (Moorlag et al., 2020).

claim: Virulent M. tuberculosis can program macrophages to attenuate bactericidal responses to subsequent mycobacterial challenge.

claim: There is extensive geographical overlap between tuberculosis endemic areas and the presence of helminths.

claim: Parasites induce type 2 responses, leading to alternative macrophage activation.

claim: Products of the helminth Fasciola hepatica can train murine macrophages for enhanced secretion of IL-10.

claim: On Day 0, M(4/13) displayed comparable killing capacity to naive M(-).

claim: Following BCG infection on Day 0, no IL-10 secretion was detected.

claim: Following BCG infection on Day 0, only bactericidal M(IFNγ/LPS) secreted detectable levels of TNFα.

claim: On Day 6, M(4/13) exhibited heightened mycobacterial uptake.

claim: M(4/13) exhibited heightened expression of CD206, MHC II, Arg1, Chil3, and Retnla.

claim: In mice, the induction of iNOS is important for bactericidal NO production and subsequent killing of M. tuberculosis.

evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Flynn et al., 1993 and Pasula et al., 2017.

claim: Arg1 directly impedes the bactericidal function of iNOS by sequestering arginine.
source: In turn, Arg1 directly impedes the bactericidal function of iNOS by sequestering the amino acid, arginine, which each enzyme uses to make their respective products: ornithine and NO.

claim: In the murine model of TB infection, Arg1 has been linked with increased bacterial burden and pathology.

claim: M(IFNγ/LPS) exhibited markedly higher expression of Nos2 compared with M(4/13).

claim: Following stimulation with Mtb, trained M(4/13) exhibited equivalent expression of Arg1 compared with untrained M(-).

claim: Following stimulation with Mtb, trained M(4/13) exhibited enhanced Nos2 expression compared with untrained M(-).

claim: M(4/13) on Day 1 displayed both an increase of oxygen consumption rate (OCR) and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR).

claim: Upon secondary stimulation on Day 6 with Mtb, M(IFNγ/LPS) showed reduced transcription of Sdha.
